content:
Chapter revision shows what your child knows. A mixed paper shows what they can DO in 60 minutes. Those are very different things. The real IMO never asks thirty rational-number questions in a row. It jumps from interest to a cylinder to a coding puzzle. That switching is a skill of its own. So take the free IMO Class 8 practice test below. It has 10 questions from ten different Class 8 chapters, with instant scoring and worked explanations.

Why mixed practice beats one more chapter revision

  • The real paper changes topic on every question. Chapter-order drilling never trains that reflex.
  • Mixed tests expose the avoided chapter. Every student has one.
  • Time pressure only turns real against a full 30-question paper.
  • Exam-day calm comes from having "been here before" — twenty-five times.

How to use this free test

  • Attempt all 10 in one sitting, without help.
  • Score 8 or more? Move on to full papers. Below 6? Revise the weakest chapter first.
  • Read every explanation, even for the questions answered correctly.
  • Track the clock too. Ten mixed questions in 12 minutes is Olympiad pace. Under 15 is solid. Over 20 means one weak chapter steals time from the rest.

Free IMO Class 8 practice test

The quiz below mixes ten chapters. Numbers, shapes, roots, interest, identities, mensuration, proportion, graphs, number play and reasoning. That is the spread of a real IMO paper, in miniature.

One more tip: mark it honestly. No half marks, no "I nearly had it". A clean 7 with real working beats a lucky 9 every time. And the trend across three or four tests tells you far more than any single score ever will.

Then do the real thing — 25 times

The IMO Class 8 Maths — 25 Practice Papers e-book has 25 full papers — 750 MCQs. Every paper takes exactly two questions from each of the 15 chapters. An answer key follows each paper. Then come step-by-step solutions for all 750 questions. That includes 159 diagram questions with real figures, just like the exam. Chapter drills sit on the Grade 8 Math shelf. The theory is free on the vidaara.org IMO course.

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Mixed Practice Test
quiz.intro: Ten questions, ten different chapters — just like the real paper. Press Check my score at the end.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 8: mixed practice

questions.explanation: Apply the distributive property in reverse (taking 3/7 as common factor): (3/7) × (2/5) + (3/7) × (3/5) = (3/7) × (2/5 + 3/5) = (3/7) × (5/5) = (3/7) × 1 = 3/7.

questions.q: In a regular polygon, each interior angle is 5 times its exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Let the exterior angle be E. Then interior angle = 5E. Since interior + exterior = 180 degrees, 5E + E = 180, so 6E = 180, giving E = 30 degrees. Number of sides = 360/30 = 12.

questions.q: The number of perfect squares between 1 and 1000 (inclusive) that are divisible by both 4 and 9 is:
questions.explanation: A number divisible by both 4 and 9 is divisible by lcm(4, 9) = 36. A perfect square divisible by 36 must have n divisible by 6 (since 36 = 6²). So n = 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 give n² = 36, 144, 324, 576, 900 — all at most 1000

questions.q: A retailer buys a fan for Rs 1,500 and marks it 40% above the cost price. He then offers a 25% discount. Find the profit percent.
For what value of k does (x + 2) divide x³ + kx² - 4x + 12 exactly?
questions.explanation: By the factor theorem, f(-2) = 0. f(-2) = -8 + 4k + 8 + 12 = 4k + 12 = 0, so k = -3. Verify: x³ - 3x² - 4x + 12 = (x + 2)(x - 2)(x - 3).

questions.q: A trapezium ABCD has parallel sides AB = 25 cm and DC = 11 cm. The non-parallel sides AD = 13 cm and BC = 15 cm. Find the area of the trapezium.
questions.explanation: Drop perpendiculars from D and C onto AB. Let the foot from D be at distance a from A. Then AD² = a² + h² gives 169 = a² + h². The foot from C is at distance (a + 11) from A, so (25 - a - 11)² + h² = BC² gives (14 - a)²

questions.q: If P is directly proportional to Q², and P = 48 when Q = 4, find Q when P = 75.
questions.explanation: P = kQ². Substituting: 48 = k(16), so k = 3. When P = 75: 75 = 3Q², Q² = 25, Q = 5.

questions.q: A point in the fourth quadrant is 13 units from the origin. If its abscissa is 5, its ordinate is:
questions.explanation: Let the ordinate be y. Then √(5² + y²) = 13, so 25 + y² = 169, giving y² = 144 and y = +/-12. Since the point is in the fourth quadrant, y < 0. So y = -12. (This uses the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple.)

questions.q: The product of the digits of a two-digit number is 14. When 45 is added to the number, the digits are reversed. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be 10a + b. Product: ab = 14. Reversal condition: 10a + b + 45 = 10b + a, so 9(b - a) = 45, giving b - a = 5, i.e., b = a + 5. Substituting: a(a + 5) = 14, so a² + 5a - 14 = 0, giving (a + 7)(a - 2) = 0. S

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ___
questions.explanation: The positions of the letters are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15. The gaps between positions are +2, +3, +4, +5, which increase by 1 each time. The next gap is +6, so the next position = 15 + 6 = 21, which is the letter U.
